chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far informed me from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'ada ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Allah showers mercy on the father who helps his son in doing good. Allah showers mercy on the neighbor who helps his neighbor in doing good. Allah showers mercy on the companion who helps his companion in doing good. Allah showers mercy on the companion who helps his companion in doing good. Allah showers mercy on the man who helps his ruler in doing good.
ai.seo_question: What are the five relationships in which helping the other in good deeds brings Allah's mercy?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith utilizes a rhetorical chain of divine mercy to highlight the communal responsibility of facilitating righteousness (*birr*) across key social hierarchies. It extends the concept of mutual support beyond the family to include neighbors, companions, and even the political subject-ruler dynamic, reflecting the Shia emphasis on holistic social piety. This teaching underscores that true faith manifests in actively enabling others to perform good deeds, thereby multiplying collective spiritual rewards.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. al-Hassan who said I was informed by Abdillah b. Ja’far from Harun b. Muslim from Mas’ada b. Ziyad from Ja’far b. Muhammad from his father from Ameer al-Mumineen (a.s.) that he said that The Messenger of Allah (s.a.w.s.) who said: “

Allah showers mercy on the father who helps his son in doing good. He showers mercy on a person who helps his neighbor in doing good. One who helps his friend in doing good Allah showers mercy on the former. Similarly one who helps his companion in doing good, Allah showers mercy on the former too. Also one who helps his master in doing good, Allah showers mercy on that person.”
